svg.title: Step 9 · The MCP · no auth lane
svg.desc: The page's lane picker sends the lane with the question; the chat checks it against the open lanes. On REST · no auth, the tools call Open-Meteo. On MCP · no auth, the answer connects to our own MCP server on this same deployment, at an address of its own, lists the tools within 6 s and checks our four are there; each call is a tools/call within 8 s, and the server calls Open-Meteo. The chips show the lane, the JSON-RPC request as sent, and the server's request to Open-Meteo; the compare view shows one forecast call through each lane.
svg.text: Step 9 · The MCP · no auth lane
Two doors to the same four tools: the question takes the lane chosen
The page: the lane picker
REST or MCP, without auth or with it: two open,
two closed until step 10; the radios belong to
the form, so the lane goes with each question
chat.py: the lane, checked
one of the open lanes, else our sentence:
"That lane isn't open yet."
then that lane's tools, for this answer
REST · no auth (step 4)
the tools call Open-Meteo themselves
one request a call, through the cache
the chip: On the wire, the GET
8 s a call, its tries included
MCP · no auth (step 9): mcp_lane.py
one connection to /api/mcp: 6 s to list the tools
our four required; each call a tools/call, 8 s
the server (step 8) calls Open-Meteo
the chip: the JSON-RPC request, then the GET
Where the lane finds our server: never where a request says
On Vercel, the address the question came to, if it's one of the deployment's own names; else the deployment's URL.
On a computer, the address the app listens on. A bypass secret, if Vercel gives one, goes with each call, masked.
Our own wrapper: langchain-mcp-adapters' latest imports the SDK's version 1 (issue 63). The SDK's
client runs in a task group, which wraps whatever leaves it: the lane unwraps a group of one, so the chat
still knows its own errors (issue 64). The compare view shows one forecast call through each lane.
In the tests: the lane on the app's own server, in this process; six addresses, forged ones among them
Same tools, same inputs, same errors: only the door changes, and the chips show it.
MCP costs a connection and a hop a call; any MCP server's tools can be reached the same way.
